speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with jaundice, itching, weight loss, pale stools, and dark urine; to narrow down the cause of this obstructive pattern, have you noticed any pain specifically in the upper right abdomen or any history of gallstones?

speaker: Patient
text: 72-year-old male. The patient has experienced gradual yellow discoloration of the skin and generalized pruritus over the past 2 weeks. He also reports a decreased appetite and a weight loss of 6.3 kg (14 lb). The patient’s stool has been pale, and his urine is very dark. Three years ago, he had an episode of acute upper abdominal pain, which was managed with IV fluids, NSAIDs, and dietary modification. The patient has abstained from alcohol for these three years, after having consumed 1–2 beers daily for 40 year...

speaker: Doctor
text:
The patient has a history of chronic alcohol use and a prior episode of acute upper abdominal pain three years ago. Given the combination of weight loss, pruritus, and obstructive jaundice, is there a palpable mass in the right upper quadrant, or have you noticed a change in the texture of your liver?

REQUEST TEST: Liver Function Panel; REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Palpation of the right upper quadrant reveals a soft, cystic mass; no tenderness is noted. Liver texture is not explicitly described as distinct, but the mass is identified. Liver Function Panel: Bilirubin Total 5.6 mg/dL, Direct Bilirubin 4.8 mg/dL, Alkaline Phosphatase 192 U/L, AST 32 U/L, ALT 34 U/L. Abdominal Ultrasound: Anechoic cystic mass in the subhepatic region with dilation of intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Choledochal cyst (likely Type I or IV) causing obstructive jaundice. The presence of a cystic mass in the subhepatic region, combined with painless jaundice, weight loss, and significant dilation of the bile ducts on ultrasound, is highly characteristic of this condition. Given the patient's age and weight loss, malignancy arising within the cyst (cholangiocarcinoma) is a critical concern to rule out.
